correctness.rationale: An exact arcsine-pushforward change of variables yields Chebyshev coefficients and block diagonalization by harmonic degree. Direct diagonalization proves λ±=(k±|Σexp(2inφj)|)/2, and a phasor identity proves explicit torus-distance upper/lower bounds. A precise Fourier H^{-τ} eigenvalue comparison, simultaneous Dirichlet approximation, interpolation and least-eigenvector examples establish all quantifiers, sharp cutoff and optimal conditional exponent. The 450 numerical Gram tests and direct pushforward quadrature check the nonstandard normalizations, not the infinite theorems.

value.rationale: A natural finite-angle Cramér–Wold inverse problem needs quantified conditioning beyond uniqueness. The new exact all-k spectral decomposition and sharp finite-band condition number provide an actionable stability invariant; the simultaneous Diophantine threshold and optimal conditional Hölder exponent reveal how k views change the best attainable resolution. This is a motivated structural classification, not a narrow arbitrary parameter evaluation.
